newsitem.title: INDIA: India foreign investment trend worrying - economist.
newsitem.headline: India foreign investment trend worrying - economist.

text.p: A spurt in recent foreign direct investment (FDI) into consumer product industries in India was causing concern, a top economist said on Friday.

"I am concerned in the trend over the last one month," D.R. Pendse, chief consulting economist for the Industrial Development Bank of India, told a seminar on Indian business "in the emerging economic scenario".
He said about 85 percent of FDI traditionally went to high capital-intensive industries and only about 15 percent in the consumer durables sector.
But over the last month, the trend appeared to be reversing, Pendse said, citing government approvals for Indian projects of Warner Brothers, Coca Cola and BMW.
"I don't know what desperate hurry there is to approve these projects," he told the seminar organised by the India Club.
Pendse said his concern was that when these projects made profits, repatriation of profits would pose problems for India's balance of payments.

"It appears the government is concerned about achieving the $10 billion (FDI) target," he said, referring to the common minimum programme of the new government which, among other things, is committed to attracting an annual $10 billion in FDI.
Pendse said it was tragic that the power sector, so crucial to India, did not attract investments.
